newsitem.title: POLAND: Budapest leads E.Europe bourses after record surge.
newsitem.headline: Budapest leads E.Europe bourses after record surge.

text.p: The Budapest bourse led other East European exchanges this week, surging to all-time highs in heavy volume, while Prague was lifted by foreign buying.
Other bourses saw a pre-holiday drop in trade. Warsaw had slight gains in modest volumes, while Bratislava, Zagreb, Ljubljana and Bucharest slipped.
BUDAPEST
The Hungarian market rallied this week, closing with a sixth successive record high on Thursday and rapidly nearing the 4,000 point barrier.
The BUX index closed on Thursday at 3,962.16 points, up 143.95 points or 3.77 percent from last Friday.
Spot share turnover on Wednesday was worth 3.405 billion forints ($20.75 million), the second highest ever.
Traders said the fact the U.S. Federal reserve left rates steady on Tuesday helped spur the rally.
Chemicals company TVK helped lead the market this week, boosted by the news it may receive five billion forints from privatisation agency APV Rt, based on Hungary's previous privatisation law.
PRAGUE
Czech shares, especially major issues, pushed ahead on the week to Thursday. SPT Telecom wass the most heavily weighted stock.
SPT Telecom, which accounts for over 20 percent of the PX50's capitalisation, gained more than six percent.
Dealers said the stock had benefited from buying by foreign investors who had hesitated over recent weeks due to fears about a lack of transparency in the capital markets.
Traders said they could not explain the resurgence of interest from abroad in SPT.
"Interest in SPT came from abroad but I don't know why," said Ivan Kusacek of Zivnostenska Banka.
WARSAW
Polish shares rose slightly this week and analysts said the market should extend its flat trend to the Christmas holiday.
"We could have a slight rise, but there should be no big (main index) movements in prices or turnover in the pre-holiday period," said Roman Sosnowski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage.
Some analysts said the market could rise after the holiday, in part in anticipation of better first-quarter earnings.
Others said the central bank head's comments that interest rates could rise if fast credit growth continued could help cool market sentiment in January.
The main market's all-share WIG index closed on Thursday at 13,851.9 points, up 145.6 points or 1.1 percent from last Friday's close.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks were stable to lower in shrinking volume throughout the week, and analysts said the holiday season lull would continue to the end of the year.
Only the two fully listed issues, Zagrebacka Banka and drugs firm Pliva, are to remain unaffected, analysts said, while other stocks can expect lower prices and volume.
Pliva jumped 300 kuna on Thursday to 13,300 after trading flat for the past 10 days. Zagrebacka held ground at 980 kuna.
BRATISLAVA
The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) saw large volumes traded in main issues during the year's last trading week, but brokers said most of them were in previously-agreed block and direct trades.
The 12-share SAX index eased 3.04 points to close the year at 178.05 on Thursday from Monday's open at 181.09 points.
"What we saw this week were mostly only portfolio swaps, usual for the period before the end of year," Libor Briska of Creditanstalt said.
He said investors next month might show optimism after several months of lethargy, mainly due to legislative efforts to amend the securities law.
BUCHAREST

Volumes stayed light on the Bucharest bourse this week with investors already in a holiday mood. On Thursday, turnover rose by 14 million lei, but stayed low at 40 million. Prices were mixed with two independent indices hitting year lows.
Buying interest at the week's two sessions focused on Azomures SA fertiliser maker, which took the bulk of turnover and closed 500 lei stronger at 12,100 on Thursday.
The bourse's next trading is due on January 7.
Two unofficial indices, the VAB and the BIG, slipped by 1.7 percent from the previous session to year lows of 262 points and 261.36 points respectively.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares fell 1.95 percent this week with Port Luka Koper the leading decliner, falling 10.4 percent. The top gainer was bank Hipotekarna banka Brezice, rising 13.8 percent.
